extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant reviewers and immunology/thymus researchers (investigators preparing or reviewing R01-style proposals)
extracted.subtask_description: An R01-style research proposal describing specific aims, significance, innovation, and approach for studying lymphoid→stromal signaling in the thymus using an inducible mouse model and in situ stromal gene mapping. Targets reviewers and scientists evaluating experimental design, prioritization metrics, and validation strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of stromal gene expression
rubrics_metrics.description: Stromal gene expression is defined as gene expression in the tissue that is not attributable to gene expression by the corresponding lymphoid cells.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operationally implemented by measuring RNA from microdissected tissue regions and simultaneously measuring gene expression in lymphocytes corresponding to those regions; stromal genes are those remaining after removing lymphoid-attributable signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of IL7R-/- inducible thymic growth model
rubrics_metrics.description: Use an inducible model of thymus growth represented by IL7R-/- mice transplanted with wildtype lineage-negative bone marrow/stem cells.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justification: stromal cells are inherently normal in IL7R-/- mice, the thymus undergoes profound growth without myeloablative conditioning, and the unmanipulated IL7R-/- thymus retains visible cortical and medullary regions allowing baseline measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling at defined growth phases
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze stromal gene expression at key time points corresponding to growth induction, log phase growth, termination of growth, and steady-state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These discrete phases enable dynamic characterization of stromal responses over the induced growth trajectory.

rubrics_metrics.name: In situ differential stromal gene mapping methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Use microdissection of tissue regions (cortex, medulla, or other regions) followed by cDNA microarray profiling to identify stromal gene expression in situ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advantages listed: no changes caused by disruption of 3D context or enzymatic digestions, non-biased detection of all stromal cells in a region, requires very little tissue (amenable to hypotrophic tissues).

rubrics_metrics.name: Matched simultaneous measurement of lymphoid and stromal expression
rubrics_metrics.description: Simultaneously measure gene expression in microdissected tissue and in corresponding sorted lymphoid cells from matched anatomical regions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This paired measurement is required to separate stromal expression from lymphoid-derived expression in the tissue sample.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replication standard for microarrays
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform three independent microarrays for each sample type (cortical or medullary, tissue or lymphoid).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each microarray will represent pooled RNA; three independent arrays provide replication for expression measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of stromal receptors as candidate mediators
rubrics_metrics.description: From stromally expressed genes, identify those that encode receptors as candidate stromal mediators of lymphoid-derived signals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These stromal receptor genes will form the receptor list to be cross-validated with lymphoid ligands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation criterion: presence of ligand in lymphoid cells
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify the presence of the corresponding ligand in lymphoid cells at corresponding phases of the growth response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This verification is used to support receptor:ligand candidate validity (i.e., receptor present in stroma and ligand present in lymphoid cells during the same phase).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative prioritization metric — receptor:ligand co-citation frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: Use frequency of receptor:ligand co-citation (higher co-citation indicates greater biological relevance) as a quantitative metric for prioritization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Co-citation frequency will be captured computationally from literature/databases and contributes to an overall priority score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative prioritization metric — thymus-specific co-citation frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure frequency of co-citation of receptor or ligand in reference to the thymus (low thymus citations can be interesting when paired with high co-citation scores).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This metric helps flag novel or understudied axes that nevertheless show strong receptor:ligand association.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative prioritization metric — co-occurrence in public databases
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess co-occurrence of receptor and ligand entries across public databases as evidence supporting the pairing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Co-occurrence across multiple databases increases confidence in functional relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative prioritization metric — experimental evidence (database driven)
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate experimental evidence drawn from databases as a quantitative metric indicating prior experimental support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experimental-database support strengthens prioritization and will be integrated computationally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative prioritization metric — ANOVA p value for dynamic response
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the ANOVA p value (for the dynamic response range of individual receptors) as a statistical metric of expression dynamics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ANOVA p values quantify whether receptor expression changes significantly across sampled time points; included in the overall scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall priority scoring and score combination
rubrics_metrics.description: Derive an overall priority score using a combination of the quantitative metrics, although individual scores may be used independently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computational combination produces ranked candidates; downstream manual review may override or refine rankings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative prioritization criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply qualitative assessments including availability of genetic mutant resources, modulatory compounds or molecular reagents, and analytical reagents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These qualitative factors influence feasibility of biological validation and translational follow-up and are considered alongside quantitative scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data integration and provenance standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop all metrics computationally and merge them into a single database including hypertext links to relevant resources (literature citations, experimental databases, mouse mutant repositories, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This supports traceability, reproducibility, and rapid access to supporting evidence for each candidate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final prioritization decision rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Final priorities will be determined by manually evaluating qualitative metrics in the context of the highest-scoring candidates from quantitative analysis, with particular emphasis on the availability of mouse models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manual expert judgment integrates practicality (e.g., available mutants) with computational scores to select candidates for validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biological validation standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish biological relevance for top candidates by evaluating thymic size and composition directly in receptor (stromal) or ligand (lymphoid) mutant mouse models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides proof-of-concept and the basis for mechanistic follow-up studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of non-myeloablative induction to avoid artefacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Induce thymic growth without myeloablative conditioning to avoid damaging effects of ablative regimens on thymic stromal cells.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoiding chemical/radiological conditioning preserves stromal integrity and produces more physiologically relevant stromal responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for anatomically organized baseline thymus
rubrics_metrics.description: Select model or samples where the thymus contains visible and organized cortical and medullary regions to allow establishment of baseline gene expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Models lacking such organization are unsuitable for baseline-region-specific stromal mapping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological advantage criteria for stromal mapping
rubrics_metrics.description: Method should be non-biased, preserve 3D context, return information on all stromal cells in a region, and require very little tissue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These features are specifically cited as advantages of the proposed microdissection + microarray approach and are criteria for method choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personnel and effort expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: PI and named personnel commitments: PI responsible for 100% support of own salary and fringe and oversight duties; PI effort 1.2 calendar months; post-doctoral fellow 12 calendar months; informatic scientist 1.2 calendar months (with intensive effort months 7–12).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Roles include supervision, training, data review prior to publication, manuscript writing, and budget/protocol/reporting responsibilities; staffing and effort are part of feasibility and management review.
